notes.title: The Magic of Voice Acting - Interview with Sally Beaumont 🎙
notes.content:
Hey everyone, 

Gameplay, mechanics, and art direction are all crucial to game development, but the contribution of stellar voice acting often goes unnoticed. Perhaps that’s intentional! The best voice acting blends into the overall soundscape of a game, helps set the scene, and brings characters to life. Voice acting that makes itself obvious can ruin immersion.

How do we bring Lord Winklebottom Investigates’ characters to life, and what do our voice actors have to say about their profession?

We’re shining a spotlight on one such incredible actress, [url=https://twitter.com/sallybeaumont1]Sally Beaumont[/url], the talented voice behind numerous stars of Lord Winklebottom Investigates. Here’s what she had to say.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34478666/4df70f9cdb78e73dd0ba29f74646ca27e6b52262.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34478666/bdeae1d22de79d13162acd8f6401498891662f72.png[/img][/url]

[h3]How long have you been voice acting? How did it all start?[/h3]
I’d probably say I’ve been voice acting since I could speak. Realising it was a real job happened in my late teens, and I have been hooked ever since. I trained at University, and acting was all about transformation. When I learned how to use the studio there, I was able to transform even more!

[h3]Which Lord Winklebottom Investigates characters did you voice?[/h3]
I’m Dame Celia, Beryl the Maid, and another TOP SECRET role. You’ll have to play the game to meet her.

[h3]Which one was the most fun and challenging to record and why?[/h3]
Oh gosh. Dame Celia is an absolute hoot! We pushed her flamboyance about as far as it could go! Beryl is also a fabulous role. I love Agatha Christie maids, the type who drop the tea tray and screech when they discover the body, so Beryl was wonderful fun. It’s such a lively, well-written script that the characters kind of sprang out of me.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34478666/a63c2bdbbfea0f5416e1399e7d801ff9f2b58b46.gif[/img]

[h3]What's it like working on Lord Winklebottom Investigates?[/h3]
Honestly? Absolute joy. I love the concept and am an avid Conan Doyle fan, so I was keen to play a suspect. The comedy references it makes speak to me- Carry On films, Fawlty Towers, Round The Horn. The team are smashing, too. They know exactly what they want from the voices, which makes life much easier. Oh, and they laugh at my ridiculous performances, encouraging me to go even further!

[h3]Can you tell me a little bit about your all-time favourite projects?[/h3]
It’s usually whatever I’m working on right now—I love the process of getting to know a new character. I loved working on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/489930/Adventures_of_Bertram_Fiddle_2_A_Bleaker_Predicklement/]Bertram Fiddle 2[/url]; it clicked with me how much I wanted to work in adventure games. [url=https://stairfallinstitute.itch.io/aye-fair-lady]Aye Fair Lady[/url] was also a pivotal moment, Charlotte Gore encouraged me to be very silly, and it’s the role many people remember me from. Oh, and Carlata from [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1037120/Mutropolis/]Mutropolis[/url]. She’s a lot like me, and I love that she’s this funny, complicated woman who gets underestimated a lot. I think a lot of actresses would get that!

[h3]What's the best part about voice acting?[/h3]
Joke answer: working in my pyjamas (actually, no, maybe I’m not joking).
Real answer: I get to work on lots of different things at once, many different challenges, and I get to be part of a team that makes magic happen. I think games can be magic, especially for players.

[h3]What is the biggest challenge of your job?[/h3]
I think the feast/famine nature of the job is really tough—not just on your finances and energy levels but your self-esteem too. Having work dry up can leave you feeling like you’re all washed up, and then the next week, you’re overwhelmed. So I try to have personal and professional goals that aren’t in the hands of others. I can take care of my voice, feed my creativity, and support the VA community. That all helps.

[h3]How do you bring a character to life?[/h3]
It varies depending on the role, but often I find out what that character finds funny. Sometimes a laugh will make a character click. I like to listen to people generally and try to bring real intonations I’ve heard to a role. It’s kind of alchemical sometimes. You’ll do a take, and the developer will make eye contact, and you’ll both feel it—that’s the character.

[h3]What does successful voice acting sound like to you? [/h3]
It doesn’t sound like anything! What I mean is, if you’re thinking, “cor! That’s some good voice acting!” then that isn’t good. It’s pulling you out of the story. It should feel effortless, right. Good voice acting follows the overall goals of the game developer whilst bringing a little extra something that’s unique to the performer.


Which character voice are you most excited about? Why? Leave a comment below and let us know!


More from Sally Beaumont:

[previewyoutube=bUDUbUf_4Lc;leftthumb][/previewyoutube] [previewyoutube=vDh20azGpEA;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Let's Talk Gameplay!
notes.content:
Hey guys,

With the official release of [i]Lord Winklebottom Investigates[/i] just around the corner, I thought now would be the perfect time to take a closer look at some of its defining gameplay elements.

In case you didn’t know already, [i]Lord Winklebottom Investigates[/i] is a whodunnit point and click with a twist—or two. Players assume the role of Lord Winklebottom, a giraffe detective tasked with solving the mysterious murder of his childhood friend, Admiral Gilfrey. 

There are hundreds of clickable elements scattered around the Isle of Barghest, serving all kinds of different uses and functions.

Throughout your journey, you’ll come across useful tools and objects that you can:

[list]
[*] Use at the right time and place to solve challenging puzzles. There’s no pixel hunting in [i]Lord Winklebottom Investigates[/i], which means players don’t have to position their cursor perfectly to interact with chosen elements.
[*] Combine to create new items. Some puzzles require you to drag one object/tool in your inventory and drop it onto another.
[*] Share with suspects to unlock new interactions. Again, this is done by dragging items and dropping them where necessary.
[/list]
It’s all about timing and careful observation. Random clicking won’t get you anywhere, so you need to pay close attention to everything that transpires on the island. You can access Winklebottom’s journal with his notes at any time, but you can also keep your own notes as you learn more about the story.

You’re also free to roam around, and you’ll soon discover that new interactions with suspects become available as your knowledge grows. Exploration is encouraged, and if you want to crack the case, you’ll have to venture beyond the gates of Gilfrey’s manor.

[b]Do you have what it takes to find Gilfrey’s killer?[/b]

[i]Lord Winklebottom Investigates[/i] is coming to [url=bit.ly/Winklebottom]Steam[/url] very soon. Download the preview demo, and don’t forget to join our enthusiastic [url=discord.gg/cavemonsters]discord community[/url] today! 

See you soon! 🦒

notes.title: The Animal Question 🦒
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

[i]Lord Winklebottom Investigates[/i] will soon hit the digital shelves, but we still haven’t addressed the giraffe in the room: [b]What’s with the animals?[/b]

The world of [i]Lord Winklebottom Investigates[/i] draws heavily from the classic mystery novels of the early 20th century. The mysterious murder, the mansion, the suspects, the eccentric detective—all are conventional whodunnit elements with which many of you will be very familiar.

Here’s the twist. Although similar to our own reality in many ways, this world is inhabited by all kinds of conscious, talking animals. 

Talking (or otherwise anthropomorphized) animals have made many appearances in art over the centuries. They’re, of course, very popular with children. Sometimes, they’re used as symbols of different qualities and virtues; other times, they’re part of moral/political allegories. For example, George Orwell’s [i]Animal Farm[/i] is an allegorical commentary on the rise of communism in post-Czarist Russia. 

The introduction of human-like animal characters in a detective story can be pretty advantageous for several reasons:

It broadens the audience by toning down the mature elements associated with the genre. [i]Lord Winklebottom Investigates[/i] maintains all the fun and mystery of detective games without the gruesome imagery.
It provides opportunities for comedic relief and leaves plenty of room for jokes/puns/and funny references.
It allows for unique and memorable suspects, making it really easy to keep track of who’s who - valuable for Let’s Plays and live streams. Whodunnits can be hard to follow, especially when dozens of suspects are vying for attention. Distinctive animal characters help solve this problem.

But the most honest answer to the animal question is: [i]Why not?[/i] Much like humans, animals can be clever, cunning, fierce, timid, and the list goes on. The possibilities are endless, and the anthropomorphic qualities of the animals in Lord Winklebottom Investigates add a fun and playful twist to the story.

What is your favourite animal, and does it make an appearance in [i]LWI[/i]? Find out by purchasing a copy of the game once it becomes available, later in the year. Meanwhile, [url=discord.gg/cavemonsters]join our friendly discord community[/url] and share your thoughts and excitement!

notes.title: The Highs and Lows of Development 📈
notes.content:
Hi guys,

Developing an indie game from scratch can be quite a roller coaster ride. There are both highs and lows, and both have come at points with the development of Lord Winklebottom Investigates. 


[b]What have been the biggest challenges of the game's development?[/b]
[i]My first Kickstarter failed to meet its goal, but I didn’t let that get to me. I made several good contacts through game localization, sought advice, and relaunched with a more focused goal. In addition to delays caused by COVID, there have also been family health problems to contend with, as my husband, who has a heart condition, had to unexpectedly go into hospital to have an operation. One of the problems with developing the game largely solo is that when a family emergency happens, there’s nobody else to pick up the work.[/I]

[b]What have been the best parts of the game’s development?[/b]
[i]I remember I was super excited to see people play the game for the first time at AdventureX. It was a similar experience when I attended Insomnia and EGX. As a creator, nothing beats the feeling of watching people play and enjoy your game. I was also thrilled to see Lord Winklebottom Investigates running on Switch for the first time, and I got very emotional when I heard some of the characters come to life in the VO sessions.[/I]


Lord Winklebottom Investigates is in the final stages of development and set to release in early 2022. [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1024160/Lord_Winklebottom_Investigates/]Download the special preview demo[/url] (if you haven’t already), and [url=discord.gg/cavemonsters]come join our active community on Discord today[/url]! 🕹️👾

See you there!

notes.title: Games, Books and Movies. The Inspirations Behind Lord Winklebottom Investigates
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

These past few weeks have been very busy, but [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1024160/Lord_Winklebottom_Investigates/]Lord Winklebottom[/url] is no stranger to a packed schedule. As we move closer to release, I thought it’d be fun to explore some of the inspirations behind the game in a little more detail. 

There are definitely similarities between Lord Winklebottom and [b]Sherlock Holmes[/b]. They share a keen eye for suspicious activity, sticking their neck in where it’s not always wanted!. Like every good detective, Lord Winklebottom also has his own eccentricities, a bit of a dandy with his top hat, pipe, and monocle; he's a bit old-fashioned for the times he lives in. 

The figure of Dr. Frumple was inspired, of course, by Dr. Watson, Holmes’ loyal sidekick. In our case, Dr. Frumple resembles the less-than-brilliant, perhaps slightly bumbling version of Dr. Watson as portrayed by Nigel Bruce in the late 30s and early 40s. That’s no sleight on Dr. Frumple, however! He deserves just as much credit as Lord Winklebottom, something which he is only too quick to remind you of.

The game’s mysterious plot also draws inspiration from [b]Agatha Christie[/b]’s well-known classics. Players feel vulnerable and isolated on the remote Isle of Barghest, knowing that the killer must be one of the characters they’ve interacted with along their journey. They’re racing against the clock to track down this foe and solve the mystery of the Admiral’s death.

While Lord Winklebottom’s adventure comes with plenty of intrigue, thrill, and excitement, the game doesn’t take itself too seriously. The comedic undertone that permeates the story might remind you of the [b]Jeeves and Wooster[/b] stories by P.G. Wodehouse, which were first published all the way back in 1915. Other inspirations include old British comedies, such as [b]What a Carve Up[/b] and [b]The House in Nightmare Park[/b]. I don’t want to give too much away before the game is out, so I’ll stop here!

As far as gameplay is concerned, Lord Winklebottom Investigates’ streamlined point-and-click system pays homage to legendary graphic adventure games of the 90s, such as [b]The Secret of Monkey Island[/b] and [b]Grim Fandango[/b]. With their intuitive gameplay, point-and-click games allow players to solve crucial puzzles while being fully immersed in the story.

Stay tuned for more exclusive insights into the world of Lord Winklebottom Investigates!

All the best,
Charlotte

notes.title: Favourites from Tokyo Game Show 🌸
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

Last week was super exciting. We had the opportunity to attend the amazing [url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/TGS2021]Tokyo Game Show[/url] as [url=bit.ly/Winklebottom]Lord Winklebottom Investigates[/url] was selected for the “Indie Game Selected Exhibit”. 

Tons of popular games were announced during the event, but indie developers, with fresh concepts and innovative ideas, stole the show once again. Here are some interesting titles that immediately caught my eye:

[list]
[*] [b][url=https://twitter.com/NineWitchesGame]Nine Witches: Family Disruption:[/url] [/b]A puzzle game that masterfully combines witches with Nazis, magic, and the occult. Players play as Alexei Krakovitz, a professor with psychic powers, who’s out to solve the mystery behind the darkness that has befallen the town of Sundӓe. Pixelated graphics, mystery, ghosts, and quirky humor—what else can we ask for?

[*] [b][url=https://twitter.com/SomberPixel]Night Reverie:[/url][/b] Is it a dream or a nightmare? In this puzzle adventure game, seemingly random fantasy elements make their way into a child’s home. The pixelated graphics and the uncanny atmosphere make for a truly unique experience with endless possibilities.

[*] [b][url=https://twitter.com/TrylightGames]Fate of Kai:[/url][/b] A unique adventure told through the pages of a magic book. The art looks beautiful, and the idea of having to modify thought bubbles to move the story forward is particularly clever.

[*] [b][url=https://twitter.com/CleverPlays]Operation Tango:[/url][/b] It takes two to tango, and the same is true for this co-op puzzle-solving game. Operation Tango is all about espionage, hi-tech tools, and challenges that require excellent communication. There’s a lot of fun to be had here, especially if you enjoy spy adventures and don’t mind having to team up with friends.
[/list]

Tokyo Game Show was a blast, and we’re so happy we got the chance to share our own little game with the whole world. We also noticed a steady increase in the number of demo downloads, so thanks to all who tried out Lord Winklebottom Investigates during this period!

What hidden gems did you guys discover? Let’s start a discussion.

Thank you for your continued support!

All the best,
Charlotte

notes.title: A (belated) thank-you to everyone at the Yogscast Tiny Teams Event!
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

What an exciting month it has been! If you’re not aware, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1024160/Lord_Winklebottom_Investigates/]Lord Winklebottom Investigates[/url] was featured in the Investigation & Mystery category of the [b]Yogscast Tiny Teams[/b] event.

It was a privilege to be a part of the online show, and I want to thank the Yogscast team for making sure I had all the information needed to guide me through the experience and enjoy the celebration.

Many got to see the dashing detective gentleman giraffe in action, and I’m pleased to report that quite a few more folks have downloaded and played the limited release demo over the past few weeks.

Transitioning from physical to fully digital events hasn’t been easy, but like everyone else, I’ve taken the time to adapt, making the most of every opportunity. The good news is that the game is getting exposed to a wider audience, which means that overall, it’s probably reaching more people as a result of these digital events.

The Tiny Teams week-long celebration was a unique experience, bringing small indie developers together and showcasing a range of unique titles. 

I have a few favourites I enjoyed during the show! From other categories, the beautiful world of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1454640/A_Tale_of_Paper/]A Tale of Paper[/url] definitely stood out. The platformers [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1325900/Demon_Turf/]Demon Turf[/url] and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1442520/Akatori/]Akatori[/url] looked like a ton of fun as well!

From Winklebottom’s own category, I absolutely loved the quirkiness of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1185380/The_Season_of_the_Warlock/]The Season of the Warlock[/url], the stylish 30s setting of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1546920/Overboard/]Overboard![/url], and the pixelated awesomeness of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/368390/The_Darkside_Detective/]The Darkside Detective[/url]. I can’t deny the appreciation for non-humanoid detectives, which is exactly why [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/963000/The_Haunted_Island_a_Frog_Detective_Game/]Frog Detective[/url] will always hold a special place in my heart.

Once again, a big thanks to the Yogscast team for hosting an amazing event and to every one of you for your continuous support. Stay tuned, and rest assured there will be more exciting news about the game in the near future.

All the best,
Charlotte

notes.title: Lord Winklebottom Investigates sticks its neck (and demo) out for crowdfunding
notes.content:
Frog Detectives? Pah, amateurs. We all know that the most respected of all animal sleuths is the humble (if very tall and glad you noticed) Giraffe Investigator. Lord Winklebottom Investigates is an amusingly daft point and click adventure, as British as it is zoological. Imagine if Sherlock Holmes was a giraffe (and not just thinking he was after an opium bender), and Watson was a hippo and you’re most of the way there. Now take a look at this here Kickstarter page, where developers Cave Monsters hope to raise enough to finish the game. Also try the demo here, and see a trailer below.
